title: Find live hosts on a subnet
summary: Learn which addresses respond before spending time on port scans. ARP discovery is the most reliable on a local segment; ICMP and TCP probes cover routed networks.
notes: Save every scan with -oA so results can be re-parsed later and attached to the report.

title: Scan all TCP ports on a host
summary: A full 65,535-port sweep finds services that top-1000 scans miss. Run it first, then feed the open ports into a targeted service scan.
caution: A raised --min-rate can overwhelm fragile devices. Drop it for embedded or legacy systems.

title: Identify services and versions
summary: Run version detection and the default scripts against only the ports that were open. The output drives every later choice about what to enumerate.
notes: Keep the XML output; searchsploit can read it directly in the vulnerability analysis phase.

title: Enumerate SMB shares and users
summary: List shares, users and policies exposed over SMB. Start with a null session, then repeat with any credentials found in scope.
notes: A refused null session is still a finding. Record it and move on to authenticated checks.

title: Test LDAP for anonymous binds
summary: Check whether the directory answers without credentials. A readable base DN usually reveals the domain name and naming contexts.

title: Check DNS for zone transfers
summary: An open zone transfer hands over every record in the zone. Test each name server separately, since only some may allow it.

title: Discover web directories and files
summary: Brute-force common paths to find admin panels, backups and forgotten endpoints. Match extensions to the technology the service scan reported.
caution: Thousands of requests per minute show up clearly in web logs and may trigger a WAF block.

title: Enumerate Microsoft SQL Server
summary: Pull the instance name, version and NTLM details from an exposed SQL Server, then connect with any credentials in scope.

title: Read the password and lockout policy
summary: Know the lockout threshold and observation window before any credential testing. It decides how many attempts per account are safe.
caution: One extra attempt can lock a real person out of their account. Confirm the threshold first.

title: Match service versions to known vulnerabilities
summary: Search the local Exploit-DB copy using the service scan output. This sends nothing to the target, so it is a good first pass.
notes: A version match is a lead, not a finding. Confirm the service is actually vulnerable before reporting it.

title: Run Nmap vulnerability scripts
summary: The vuln script category checks for well-known flaws such as SMB and TLS weaknesses. Useful for a quick sweep, but review each hit by hand.
caution: Some scripts can crash fragile services. Confirm the target and the script category are inside the agreed scope.

title: Scan a web server with Nikto
summary: Checks for outdated server software, risky default files and common misconfigurations. Expect false positives and verify each one.
caution: Nikto is very noisy and is detected by nearly every IDS and WAF.

title: Check a found credential against services
summary: Test a credential obtained in scope against the services that accept logins, one set at a time. Record where it works; that shows how far a single exposure reaches.
caution: Check the lockout policy first, and use only credentials that came from in-scope systems.

title: Check Linux privilege escalation paths
summary: Four quick checks cover most local escalation paths: sudo rights, SUID binaries, file capabilities and scheduled jobs.

title: Orient yourself on a Windows host
summary: Establish who you are, what the machine is and which privileges the account holds before deciding on a next step.

title: Check whether SMB signing is required
summary: Hosts that do not require SMB signing are open to relay attacks. Report each one with the setting that fixes it.
notes: Remediation: set "Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)" to Enabled through Group Policy.

title: Review TLS protocols and ciphers
summary: List the protocol versions and cipher suites a service accepts, and check the certificate. Flag SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and 1.1, weak ciphers and expired certificates.

title: Audit an SSH server configuration
summary: Check the algorithms the server offers from the outside, and the effective settings on the host if you have access.
